66625: Bone Hunter Ranger, from a nomadic tribe in the White Desert, works for The Order of Veil in exchange for the tribe's survival resources.#r The Sasin people often say the desert is barren yet rich, but for tribes on the White Desert, they've never seen where it's rich in their lifetime. Kemina might have had siblings, but none survived their first month. Of friends Kemina knew after remembering, only a handful lived to adulthood. Those growing up in the White Desert's harsh environment are skilled hunters; no one should fail the pre-coming-of-age trial. In the past century, Kemina is the only failure.#r The day after the ceremony, when tribal elders thought she perished in the sand sea, Kemina stumbled back bringing a starving manticore. To save the giant beast trapped in quicksand, Kemina abandoned her prey and ceremony, but gained a loyal big friend and became the tribe's most recognizable hunter.#r As the tribe's most talented hunter, Kemina knows the desert's temperament, understands Sasin's unwritten rules, and with manticore Saloka's help, crossing the dangerous desert is like a walk. Kemina became the White Desert's best pathfinder, the first choice for caravans crossing the desert. Thus, Kemina received The Order of Veil's invitation, becoming a follower of Nephthys, the Oracle Praiser, using her expertise to barter for richer material aid.#r Whether in the tribe or City, Kemina is the most popular. She's sunny, cheerful, passionate, friendly, frugal to stingy greed. Kemina's talent brings considerable income, but most becomes food sent to the White Desert. Occasionally buying discounted sweet dried figs is Kemina's most extravagant expense.

66630: After graduating from Hong-Yi College, Zhuge Lyu passed imperial examinations. Propelled by talent and family connections, he achieved nationwide fame at a young age. Court officials believed Zhuge Lyu would become a renowned minister, yet to their surprise, after serving as Vice Minister in the Ministry of Construction for years, he submitted a memorial condemning officials and resigned to govern Sasin. This bizarre move enraged the emperor and court. Were it not for the Zhuge Lyu family's long-standing key roles in Chen-Yuan – if not merit, at least dedication – coupled with Fucius whispering to the emperor, Zhuge Lyu would have been executed for treason. Deliberately framed by the court, his action was dismissed as madness-driven flight to barbaric lands.#nBefore departing for Bovark, Zhuge Lyu warned Fucius of Chen-Yuan's crises: crushing taxes, relentless provincial disasters, encircling foreign threats, and signs of revolts or peasant uprisings. The court still viewed Chen-Yuan as an invincible empire against Caucaid, Sasin, and Demonspawn, indulging in revelry while blind to looming catastrophe.#rZhuge Lyu yearned to aid Chen-Yuan people, yet reforming before crisis struck faced immense resistance within the system. He planned to first establish a new nation in Bovark Province, then return to reform Chen-Yuan. He even contemplated rebuilding on Chen-Yuan Empire's ruins if beyond saving, purging its entrenched ills.#rHis radical vision stunned even Fucius, who endorsed a trial in Bovark Province.#rMany young College disciples shared Zhuge Lyu's concerns, voluntarily becoming his followers. They hoped he'd find answers in Sasin and return to chart their course.

66635: Having tasted freedom and lost it, Liz Barbarossa cherished liberty all the more. At seven, she watched her Village burn. In Sasin where slave trade was legal, her mother's presentable looks and childbearing Ability fetched a high price from a plantation owner. #rA master buying a comely slave boded ill—yet mother and daughter had no choice. Growing up, Liz's mother taught her to hide her appearance and wit, avoiding the master's notice. But beauty couldn't stay concealed forever. As Liz neared adulthood and her mother aged, the master set his sights on Liz. By slave law, she was his property to use as he pleased. #rFate sometimes throws lifelines to the desperate. When legendary pirate Ez Barbarossa raided the coastal plantation, he freed Liz and her mother. The fierce girl seized a pirate's pistol and cutlass, slaughtering the master's household. Ez then gave Liz his surname, training her as heir. #rThough whispers arose about an old man adopting a near-adult daughter, Ez silenced them. He personally taught Liz naval combat Skill and pirate leadership. #rOn Liz's adulthood, Ez gifted her a ship, crewmates, and gold—then sent her sailing. "Thank me not. You seized your destiny. And fortune," he declared, "is a pirate's greatest treasure." With that, Ez vanished. Liz Barbarossa naturally succeeded Ez Barbarossa as the Gold Coast's dread-inspiring Pirate Queen.

66640: Flame-Quencher Warrior, a steadfast female guardian to Katniss, always alert to any threats against Katniss.#r Reasons for Blazespawn becoming Flame-Quencher vary wildly, but Frieda's might be one of a kind. Clad in obsidian armor, her skin still Burning with the Father God's wrath, Frieda served as Warlord of the Moltenblood Legion, her status nearly equal to Gaius Scorch's, who now commands the Legion. A child of war, Frieda led her Legion chasing ruin and carnage, demonstrating reverence and loyalty to the Father God with bones of allies and enemies. Countless lives crumbled to ash in her grasp, and more would have... but on a hunt against the Betrayer, Frieda heard the Father God's bell.#r It happened at Aktur, a fragile Betrayer outpost. Frieda herself beheaded their leader, his blood dripping onto the altar below, drawing a fleeting sigh. In that moment, she saw the Father God in the blood-red sky—bound, tortured, grieving for his children's fall and ignorance—not the shrieking... false god.#r Awakened, Frieda cast aside her weapon and tried to rouse her bloodlust-immersed Legion, but deputies captured her quickly. Labeled a Betrayer accomplice, she was sent to the Moltenblood throne. There, they stripped her obsidian piece by piece, snuffed her fire with dark arts, tortured her, and hurled her into a lava pool. Yet the lava spared her; embraced by the Father God's flames like legendary ancestors, she drifted south with the flow. Aktur survivors—those "Betrayer" she'd butchered—rescued her from the lava.#r The Flame-Quenchers trekked west, building a new sanctuary in barren wastes. After awakening, Frieda learned the truth of Blazespawn, realizing everything she believed was the false god's malicious lies. When Katniss came to New Aktur with news of Uriel, the first Flame-Quencher, Frieda joined Katniss's journey, following her to Stranger's outer lands.#r Frieda's goal is simple: kill the false god, liberate all deceived kin. Since Katniss once masterminded the Obsidian Day, toppling the Apostles Assembly, she might pull it off again. For this end, Frieda will sacrifice anyone—even herself.

Clearing ruins where souls dwelled, she founded her chapel—guarding spirits and welcoming fugitive Slaves and broken souls from Black Peaks. Her chapel became the wasteland's sole haven of peace. Rebecca despises war's emotional turbulence, yet war seems the only path to grant souls final rest.

66684: High Priest of the God of Death The Silence, Death's spokesperson in the mortal realm. Deadwalker descended to the mortal world on divine mandate to reclaim the souls of those who defy death for The Silence's domain.#r While his heart still beat and breath still came, Deadwalker began serving the God of Death. The people of Sagar worshiped The Silence, pursuing courage in facing death and its transcendent beauty. The cult of The Silence permeated Sagar life—trade, rituals, warfare. Back then he bore a mortal name: Ismail. Then he brought peace, not Fear.#r The Molten Catastrophe shattered Sagar's silence. Demonspawn invaded the fertile valley, vibrant HP turning to rotten mud under iron boots. With endless molten tides cutting off reinforcements, the last army of Sagar fell like wheat before a scythe before him. As high priest of The Silence's cult, he invoked the Deity to bring impartial death.#r The Silence answered. Its miracle scorched the valley into a deadland where no living being could draw breath. Yet he did not truly die—The Silence reawakened his consciousness, granting him the honor to serve at its side. For millennia the God of Death never meddled in mortal realms, but this time it had other plans. Deadwalker replaced Ismail, returning to this land where he felt a Stranger to enforce the God of Death's will. Death is a sublime order, and he is its judge and guardian. Death is not Evil—it is simply indifferent to human affairs.
